name: Histogram
reader_question: How is one measure distributed across many items, and where does a reference value fall in it?
relationship: Frequency of one continuous measure in contiguous, equal-width bins.
use_when: One measure is observed on many items and the overall shape matters
A reference value is to be located within the distribution
avoid_when: Groups are to be compared — use box-interval or strip-plot
Items must be identified individually — use ranked-dot or ranked-bar
Fewer than about 30 observations, where bin shape is unstable

data_contract.notes: What is binned (with unit) and what is counted
Contiguous, equal-width, strictly increasing bins; counts are whole numbers ≥ 0
Optional reference value, inside the binned range

units: x axis in the measure's unit with one stated bin width; y axis is a count starting at zero.

editable: Native column chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data) for the counts
Column colour, gap and value labels
not_data_bound: Bin-edge labels, axis titles and the reference line are positioned from the fixture and do not move if bins are edited
Category names in the workbook are bin ranges; the visible edge labels are separate text boxes

table_alternative: A frequency table of bin ranges and counts.
variations: Share-of-items axis when sample sizes differ across panels
limitations: Bin width and edge convention change the visual shape; both are stated
Equal-width bins only, so column height equals frequency
Reference line is positioned and does not follow data edits

excluded_alternatives.reason: A smoothed curve implies values between observations and hides the sample size
Column height would no longer equal frequency without density rescaling
